Chapter 5: Maintaining Freedom—Daily Practices for Ongoing Spiritual Health
So, you’ve reached a milestone—experiencing real deliverance. But here’s the thing: the journey doesn’t stop there. Just like recovering from an illness means you’ve got to keep looking after your health, lasting spiritual freedom needs daily attention and intentional habits.
It’s not just about a one-time breakthrough. Spiritual freedom is both a precious gift and an ongoing responsibility. Every day, you make choices that either protect or nurture that freedom—or put it at risk.
Let’s talk about a few key habits that really help keep that freedom alive.
First, there’s consistent prayer. Think of it as the lifeblood of spiritual health. Prayer isn’t only for crisis moments—it’s how you stay connected, get guidance, and express your gratitude.
Then, there’s engaging with sacred texts. Immersing yourself in spiritual teachings gives you nourishment and protection. These words offer wisdom, encouragement, even correction—helping you keep your thoughts and actions in line with what’s true.
And let’s not forget the power of community. Trying to go it alone can leave you vulnerable to old habits creeping back in. But when you’re part of a supportive group—a faith community, a small circle of friends, or even just a trusted companion—you get encouragement, fresh perspective, and real accountability.
Ongoing self-examination is another important step. Taking regular time to reflect helps you spot where old patterns might be resurfacing, or where new challenges are popping up. It’s kind of like a routine health check-up. Catching things early makes all the difference.
And here’s something to really pay attention to: guarding against new open doors. Imagine your spiritual freedom like a house you’ve worked hard to protect. You need to stay alert—watching your choices, your relationships, and what you let influence you—so nothing slips in to compromise that freedom.
Now, let’s be honest—setbacks happen. Even with the best intentions, you might hit new challenges or find yourself slipping back into old habits. But don’t get discouraged. What matters is how you respond. When you notice things slipping, you can always return to the basics: confession, repentance, forgiveness, and letting go of old lies. That’s how you restore your freedom and keep moving forward.
I love the metaphor the book uses—it’s like tending a garden. Once you’ve cleared out the weeds and planted new seeds, you can’t just walk away. You’ve got to water, prune, and protect what’s growing. If you neglect it, the weeds come right back. But if you care for it, you’ll see real growth and fruit. Spiritual freedom works the same way—it needs constant care, but that’s what brings lasting change.
Here’s the real takeaway: don’t see these daily practices as a burden. They’re an opportunity to grow, every single day. Each day is a fresh chance to deepen your freedom, build stronger relationships, and experience more peace and purpose. It’s a journey, for sure—but with the right tools and support, lasting transformation is absolutely possible.
